notes: Pols Potten (SFCC storefront) exposes a top-level main-nav item 'New Collection' (/en/new-collection/, Dutch equivalent slug /nieuwe-collectie/ confirmed in sitemap) with a real product grid: H1 'New Collection', 130 Results header, footer 'Showing 18 of 130 results' - confirmed a genuine PLP (product tiles with data-pid, e.g. /en/sandglass-ball---xxs/110-300-216.html), not editorial/lookbook. The nav exposes 3 genuine children under the same 'New Collection' menu, each its own real PLP with an independent, distinct result count (verified via each page's own 'N Results' header + 'Showing X of N results' footer, matching exactly): Spring Summer 2026 (30), Fall/Winter 2025 (71), La Marzocco (9). Sub-counts (30+71+9=110) do not sum to the parent total (130), consistent with the parent listing including additional newest items beyond these three named drops plus some drop overlap; kept parent + 3 children as separate rows per brief Sec.3 (genuine site sub-structure), not treated as an error. La Marzocco is flagged: it is nested in the New Collection nav (not the separate Design Collabs nav) and is a real, independent product listing of presumably-newest items for that brand partnership, but its own H1 is just the brand name with no explicit 'new'/season wording on the page itself - included per the site's own placement but flagged per brief Sec.3 'COLLECTION pages need inspection' since it borders on a brand/designer listing rather than a pure new-arrivals drop. Checked main nav, footer, and sitemap_3-category.xml/sitemap_4-content.xml for other New Arrivals-type terms (New In, Just In, Latest, Nieuw, Nieuwkomers) - none found beyond the New Collection family. Site's own search returned an unpopulated default template for all queries (client-side AJAX results not visible to SSR fetch), so it was not relied on as proof of absence for any other candidates - nav + sitemap enumeration was exhaustive and sufficient.
